query: FeNiCrCoCu is considered promising for high-heat wear-resistant use and is suitable for thin-film applications; because bulk preparation is expensive, applying it as a coating on a conventional metal is more practical. Earlier studies reported improved wear or mechanical performance from high-entropy-alloy coatings on Al, Ni, and titanium-alloy substrates, and simulations of FeNiCrCoCu on Cu indicated that sliding speed affects tangential and normal forces. Other work associated composition and grain size with changes in wear damage. However, most prior studies examined a limited operating regime or the properties of the alloys themselves rather than the overall wear resistance of coatings under varied thermal conditions. Subject to retaining FeNiCrCoCu as a coating on a Cu matrix, what single intervention could improve its overall wear resistance during sliding across varied thermal and contact regimes? Present one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its causal mechanism, the predicted outcome relative to an unchanged coating in matched tests, the boundaries within which it should hold, supporting evidence from the introduction, and an experiment with a clear rejection criterion for both the predicted outcome and the proposed mechanism.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a grain refinement mechanism through optimized rotational speed during the application of the FeNiCrCoCu coating on a Cu substrate will improve its overall wear resistance during sliding across varied thermal and contact regimes.
generation.material_initial_state: FeNiCrCoCu coating on a Cu substrate
generation.intervention: Optimized rotational speed during coating application
generation.mechanism: Improved grain refinement leads to enhanced wear resistance
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved wear resistance compared to an unchanged coating in matched tests
generation.baseline: Unchanged FeNiCrCoCu coating on a Cu substrate
generation.boundary: Within the range of feasible rotational speeds for coating application
generation.uncertainty: The exact relationship between rotational speed, grain refinement, and wear resistance may vary depending on specific conditions

falsification_experiment.design: Comparative wear resistance testing of FeNiCrCoCu coatings applied with different rotational speeds
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If no significant correlation between rotational speed, grain refinement, and wear resistance is found, the hypothesis is falsified

cited_evidence.text: Gap and lever. Type: tradeoff. Statement: Higher rotational speeds (1800 rpm) achieve superior grain refinement and oxidation resistance but result in a bimodal grain distribution and a significant reduction in the fraction of high-angle grain boundaries compared to lower speeds.. System: AlCoCrFeNi High Entropy Alloy. Lever: rotational speed (strain rate). Quote: "The fraction of high angle grain boundaries (HAGBs, θ > 15°) is reduced from nearly 87% for the as-cast sample to ∼82% and 66% for the SFP_400 and SFP_1800 samples, respectively."
